original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Source-authenticated optional exact integer-pair K-rank adapter for the complete retained Eisenstein PR2017 replay; preserve every original check and full output.
scope_change_reason: Refine the replay-runtime card to the measured exact K-rank bottleneck of one complete retained Eisenstein verifier; keep its full coverage and compare the identical fixture.
bottleneck_link: The instrumented complete replay spends most time in exact rank/Fraction arithmetic. Faster full source-bound replay reduces review latency without cached success or skipped mathematical checks.
stop_rule: Stop after exact row-operation proof, every actual K-call comparison, full-output equality, independent rational restriction checks, measured same-fixture speedup, source/mutation controls and peer review.
evidence: RESULT.json: all 359 K calls agree, 311 F4 and 209 Q calls unchanged, complete output and seven retained controls preserved. Independent 9,009 matrices pass. BENCHMARK.json: full median 1.43271 s to 1.20969 s, K-call median 0.485263 s to 0.057389 s, six alternating pairs after warmup; frozen timing inputs match the actual-call digest.
author: ywz65
ai_assistance: Substantial: OpenAI Codex profiled, derived and implemented the adapter, wrote proof/checks/metadata and assisted review. Separate agent review is not independent human review.

open_questions.question: Does the adapter improve other complete Eisenstein replay fixtures?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The same quadratic field occurs elsewhere, but this benchmark covers one complete verifier.
open_questions.first_step: Capture each complete actual-call sequence and full receipt, then compare both engines.
open_questions.blocked_by: Other fixtures and their source/coverage contracts have not been checked.

open_questions.question: Can fraction-free rational elimination reduce the remaining Q-call cost?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 209 rational calls remain a substantial retained cost.
open_questions.first_step: Profile that path and preserve every exact call result and complete output.
open_questions.blocked_by: This adapter changes only the K field.

open_questions.question: Where does integer coefficient growth outweigh the saved Fraction operations?
open_questions.why_it_matters: No general runtime dominance follows from the small-rank retained matrices.
open_questions.first_step: Measure rank, dimensions and coefficient heights on large rational-pair matrices.
open_questions.blocked_by: No all-input complexity or general speed claim is established.

overlap.distinction: Exact K-rank acceleration of the full PR2017 verifier. PR2537 handles rational nullspace output in a different initializer; PR2552 handles exact Taylor ceiling arithmetic; PR2506 caches native P104 matrix-vector work. No same source/field adapter found in checked metadata.
overlap.limitations: Complete cached PR/Discussion metadata plus source bodies and local packages, not every code diff or unposted investigation.
